features.summary: Firefox’s WebRTC negotiation now handles unfamiliar media types more consistently, preserving their identifiers and allowing their SDP sections to be reused. It also honors a remote device’s H.264 frame-size and bitrate limits when they differ from the limits implied by its profile, helping peers agree on compatible video settings.

features.summary: ICE, the process WebRTC uses to find a working network path, now signals when candidate gathering is complete even if it cannot start. The other changes remove unused connection helpers and tighten where network-URI changes are allowed, simplifying transport code without changing user-facing features.

This simplifies communication between the browser and its media transport while keeping the public RTCPeerConnection API intact; the remaining changes modernize internal C++ code.
